name: University of Minnesota

profile.address: Dinkytown Greenway, Prospect Park, Stadium Village, University, Minneapolis, Hennepin County, Minnesota, 55455
profile.reading:
The Advanced Operations Center is a data infrastructure facility built by the University of Minnesota on its Twin Cities East Bank campus in Minneapolis, sited at the north end of parking lot C33, northwest of Huntington Bank Stadium. According to the university's own capital project materials, the building totals about 34,000 gross square feet, of which roughly 12,000 square feet is dedicated network and data hall space, with the remainder given over to supporting mechanical, electrical, and operational areas. The University of Minnesota's capital project management office lists a total project budget of 72.75 million dollars for the facility. Construction began in August 2024, with DLR Group serving as architect and McGough Construction as general contractor, and the project was projected for completion around August 2026.

The stated purpose of the Advanced Operations Center is to modernize and consolidate the university's core network operations infrastructure, replacing aging, dispersed facilities with a single purpose built home for the systems that keep the university's data network, and by extension much of its research, instructional, and administrative computing, running. This is university owned and operated infrastructure built to serve the University of Minnesota system itself, not a commercial colocation or wholesale data center offering capacity to outside tenants, which is consistent with how large research universities typically approach their core network and enterprise computing needs once a campus outgrows older, scattered server rooms.

Because the university's own projected completion date falls close to the time this profile was written, the facility's final operational status, including whether it has been fully commissioned and whether its network and data hall capacity matches the figures published during planning, was not independently confirmed through post completion reporting. Universities do not always publish updates once a capital project transitions from construction to operation, particularly for internal infrastructure projects like this one that lack the public ribbon cutting attention given to academic buildings or athletic facilities. What is publicly documented is the planning and construction process itself, a clearly scoped, board approved capital project with a named architect, contractor, budget, and schedule, which is more transparency than is typical for enterprise data center construction generally, where operators, including many commercial ones, routinely decline to disclose budgets or building contractors at all.

profile.facility_note: Advanced Operations Center, Twin Cities East Bank campus, Minneapolis. 34,000 gross sq ft, 12,000 sq ft data hall. $72.75M budget. Construction began Aug 2024, projected completion Aug 2026 per UMN Capital Project Management.

reading:
The University of Minnesota is a public land grant research university whose Twin Cities campus straddles the Mississippi in Minneapolis and Saint Paul. It appears in this registry as an academic operator, not a commercial one, because of a single building it is putting up for its own network and computing systems, the Advanced Operations Center.

The university's Capital Project Management office publishes the project in unusual detail for enterprise infrastructure. The building is 34,000 gross square feet, of which about 12,000 square feet is network and data hall space, with the balance given to demarcation, testing and configuration rooms, offices, storage, mechanical and electrical plant, a loading dock and an equipment yard. The total project budget is 72.75 million dollars. DLR Group is the architect and McGough Construction the general contractor. Construction started in August 2024 with completion projected for August 2026. The site is the north end of East Bank parking lot C33, northwest of Huntington Bank Stadium, chosen for network access and building size, with the south half of that lot reconfigured as contract parking. The stated purpose is to consolidate and modernise core network operations, replacing dispersed and ageing rooms with one purpose built home.

Two things are worth reading carefully. First, the cost. At 72.75 million dollars for 34,000 gross square feet the project works out to roughly 2,140 dollars a gross square foot, which is high for a university building and characteristic of hardened network and electrical infrastructure rather than of office or teaching space. Second, the absence. The university publishes budget, schedule, architect and contractor, which is more than most commercial operators disclose, but it publishes no electrical numbers at all. There is no critical IT load, no utility service figure, no standby generator rating and no cooling specification in the public project material, so this registry records none.

The registry's coordinates for the building were added to OpenStreetMap on 26 July 2026 by a mapper working from Hennepin County's 2026 aerial imagery together with a GPS trace, which establishes that the structure was standing and visible from the air by the middle of 2026 but says nothing about whether it had been commissioned. Because the university's own completion date sits so close to the time of writing, the operational status of the building, and whether the data hall was finished at the size published during planning, is not independently confirmed here. Universities rarely publish a closing update on internal infrastructure projects that get no ribbon cutting.

Nothing about the facility is commercial. It serves the University of Minnesota system's own research, instructional and administrative computing, it leases no space to outside tenants, and no pricing, tenancy or capacity marketing exists for it because none would.
